sections.dimensions:
The model begins with OzMart’s sales process and fixes the fact grain at one operational order item. Dimensions and measures follow that declaration, applying the four-step dimensional design method (Kimball Group, n.d.-a). Keeping this grain explicit prevents order-level and item-level quantities from being combined incorrectly (Kimball Group, n.d.-b).

FactSales has a surrogate SalesKey and a unique source OrderItemID. OrderID and ItemSequence identify the underlying transaction without separate dimensions. Required keys link each item to Customer, Product, Seller, purchase Date and two Geography roles. Customer supports exact-age segmentation and retains both raw and normalised education codes. Product combines product, subcategory and category attributes for a direct star-schema join. Seller describes the registered provider. Date exposes calendar periods through a YYYYMMDD key. Geography supplies destination and supplier-origin attributes from the same role-aware table, allowing the NSW supplier question to use origin independently of the state receiving purchases. Flattened dimensions simplify the required queries (Kimball & Ross, 2013).

The loaded snapshot comprises 137,901 items and 688,367 units. Dimension counts are 21,000 customers, 2,199 products, 100 sellers, 493 dates and 1,599 geographic role-location pairs. The 100 raw seller-location records describe only 99 unique IDs. One ID has contradictory state and address information; a single transformed UNK record preserves the uncertainty instead of selecting a preferred state. Raw conflicting rows remain auditable.

ItemQuantity and supplied LineAmount are additive. UnitSalesPrice is not an additive revenue measure. Separate raw floats, rounded amounts, price-times-quantity totals and discrepancies permit reconciliation. Freight remains null because the source supplies no values. Queries use delivered orders as a completed-sales proxy while retaining other statuses in the fact table. Revenue does not establish profit without costs. Dimensions describe the supplied snapshot; historical changes are not invented.
sections.implementation:
An independent SSIS master package sequences four CSV reference flows, seller, customer, product, two geography roles, date and fact loading. Its reset targets only the named student warehouse. Original-source SQL performs field projection; data integration occurs in SSIS transformations. Native Row Count components expose eleven destination counts.

Customer education uses Sorted inputs and Merge Join, followed by Lookup-based age integration. Derived Column retains the original education code and forms its normalised key. Product Lookups flatten category hierarchy. Customer Geography combines operational locations with state references; Seller Geography preserves the source conflict as UNK before Sort removes the transformed duplicate. The Date task derives calendar attributes and eliminates repeated dates.

FactSales integrates order attributes and dimension keys through native Lookups, failing unresolved matches rather than silently dropping rows. Data Conversion maps explicit target types (Microsoft, n.d.). Amounts are rounded to integral ten-thousandths before exact numeric division, correcting truncation observed in an earlier native run. Source floats remain unchanged. Missing freight is explicitly null. All destinations check constraints during fast loading; reset-time validation restores trust.

The final controls reconcile counts, original fields, monetary calculations, foreign-key roles and source transaction relationships. Actual backup restoration and full-row comparison provide a separate delivery check. The process uses no SQL INSERT SELECT integration.
